comment: One decision per state.db table, from porting guide rev 5.1 section 2.4 and the owners in section 6.4. decision is preserve, replace or not_supported. owner is session, profile, gateway or executor. inGuide is false for tables the guide does not name; those decisions are provisional and need review.

async_delegations.note: Delegation state with delivery state and attempts. It is an outbox for delegation results.

compression_locks.note: Time-based lease between processes. Replaced by single-writer actor ownership plus Host.epoch(); written as expired on export.

conversation_generations.note: Monotonic generation per chat peer. Never garbage-collected: a reset would reissue a retired affinity scope.

delivery_obligations.note: Owed replies (gateway outbox). Created lazily upstream by gateway/delivery_ledger.py. The port keeps it as the reply outbox in the session actor.

gateway_heartbeats.note: Process liveness for the orphan sweep. Stays with each gateway host process; the actor has no such process.

gateway_hygiene_state.note: Gateway failure streaks, kept with the gateway router.

gateway_routing.note: Gateway routing entries, kept with the gateway router.

messages.note: Conversation rows. Keep every column, active=0 on compacted rows, and never split a tool call from its result.

messages_fts.note: FTS5 word index. Use platform FTS5 where it exists, else a side index. Regenerated, as upstream regenerates it on recovery.

messages_fts_trigram.note: FTS5 trigram index for CJK substring search. Same rule as messages_fts.

runtime_epoch.note: Owner epoch of the session authority. Replaced by the actor's own owner epoch (Host.epoch()); the epoch is exported on the way back.

session_admissions.note: Durable input queue, unique by (principal_id, target_session_id, request_id). Status set queued, started, unknown, terminal. This is the inbox; the port does not invent a second one.

session_turn_leases.note: Time-based lease between processes. Replaced by single-writer actor ownership plus Host.epoch(); written as expired on export.

sessions.note: Conversation rows. Keep every column. The profile actor keeps the list of sessions as a derived index.

state_meta.note: Key-value metadata, including FTS layout markers.

system_prompts.note: Deduplicated system prompts keyed by hash. Kept in the session actor with sessions and messages.

telegram_dm_topic_bindings.note: PROVISIONAL, not in guide 2.4. Created only when a user opts in with /topic. Telegram adapters stay in the Python gateway host, so the tables stay there. Review before milestone 1.

telegram_dm_topic_mode.note: PROVISIONAL, not in guide 2.4. Same reasoning as telegram_dm_topic_bindings.

worker_executions.note: Managed cron, child, compute and kanban runs. Statuses registered, running, unknown, terminal. Milestone 1 decides whether tool operations reuse this table or get a sibling in the executor.

worker_receipts.note: Ordered, digest-checked results of worker runs, primary key (execution_id, sequence).
